name: Mohammad Javadi Balakan
meta_description: Mohammad Javadi (MJ) Balakan is an experimental physicist who builds superconducting quantum devices. Research on topological superconductivity in Fe(Te,Se), 2D materials and silicon optoelectronics.
lead: I build and measure superconducting quantum devices. My research looks for topological superconductivity, a route to fault-tolerant qubits, in nanoscale rings of the iron-based superconductor Fe(Te,Se).
now: Research Scientist at a stealth-mode startup in San Jose, California. Previously at SUNY Albany (CNSE) and the University of Tehran.

spotlight.title: Topological superconductivity for quantum computing
spotlight.text: Topological superconductors can host Majorana modes, the building block of qubits that resist errors by design. I fabricate hBN-encapsulated rings of the iron-based superconductor Fe(Te,Se), a few hundred nanometres across, and measure them at a few kelvin with low-noise electronics.

results.t: Half-quantum flux oscillations, the signature of half-integer phase winding
Coherent electron interference along the edges of a superconducting ring
A built-in magnetization of the superconducting condensate (PRB Letter, Editors' Suggestion)
